extracted.intended_audience: communications professionals, corporate public relations practitioners, Page Society members and organizational leaders
extracted.subtask_description: High-level ethical and practice-oriented principles for corporate public relations and communications professionals, prescribing how organizations should communicate, act, and engage stakeholders. Focuses on truthfulness, action-backed claims, stakeholder listening, long-term management, enterprise-wide responsibility, workforce ambassadorship, and composure in crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the truth.
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the public know what's happening with honest and good intention; provide an ethically accurate picture of the enterprise's character, values, ideals and actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications should be transparent and honest; avoid misleading statements or omission of material facts. Aim to present an ethically accurate portrayal of the organization's values and behavior so stakeholders can form informed opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prove it with action.
rubrics_metrics.description: Public perception of an enterprise is determined 90 percent by what it does and 10 percent by what it says.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align organizational behavior with communicated commitments. Claims must be backed by observable actions and policies; communications should reflect and reinforce real organizational practice rather than serve as window dressing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen to stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.description: To serve the enterprise well, understand what the public wants and needs and advocate for engagement with all stakeholders. Keep top decision makers and other employees informed about stakeholder reaction to the enterprise's products, policies and practices. To listen effectively, engage a diverse range of stakeholders through inclusive dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement two-way, inclusive engagement processes; gather and surface stakeholder feedback to senior leaders and employees. Treat listening as an active management function—identify stakeholders, solicit diverse perspectives, and ensure insights inform decisions and communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage for tomorrow.
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate public reaction and eliminate practices that create difficulties. Generate goodwill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be proactive and forward-looking: assess potential public responses, remove or change practices likely to cause harm or reputational risk, and pursue actions that build long-term trust and goodwill rather than short-term advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct public relations as if the whole enterprise depends on it.
rubrics_metrics.description: No strategy should be implemented without considering its impact on stakeholders. As a management and policymaking function, public relations should encourage the enterprise's decision making, policies and actions to consider its stakeholders' diverse range of views, values, experience, expectations and aspirations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed PR into strategic decision-making. Evaluate every initiative for stakeholder impact and ensure communications/PR counsel influence corporate policy and strategy to reflect stakeholder considerations across the enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realize an enterprise's true character is expressed by its people.
rubrics_metrics.description: The strongest opinions — good or bad — about an enterprise are shaped by the words and deeds of an increasingly diverse workforce. As a result, every employee — active or retired — is involved with public relations. It is the responsibility of corporate communications to advocate for respect, diversity and inclusion in the workforce and to support each employee's capability and desire to be an honest, knowledgeable ambassador to customers, friends, shareowners and public officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in internal communications, training, and culture so employees can act as credible ambassadors. Promote diversity, equity and inclusion as part of reputation management; support employees to speak knowledgeably and honestly about the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain calm, patient and good-humored.
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay the groundwork for public relations successes with consistent and reasoned attention to information and stakeholders. When a crisis arises, remember, cool heads communicate best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain composure and a steady, measured approach in both routine and crisis communications. Build relationships and trust over time through consistent attention; in crises prioritize calm, clear, and reasoned messaging rather than reactive or emotional responses.
